Small business = MORE risk. 
Big dreams = LESS risk.

Sab sochte hain ki bada business karna risky hota hai.
But the truth? It’s the complete opposite.

Chhoti dukaan wala din bhar dukaan pe baithta hai. Khud hi worker, khud hi boss. 

Ek din beemar pada business band. 
Ek wrong decision and sab khatam.
And on the other side? Bade businesses wale yacht pe ghoom rahe hain.

Why? 

Because they stopped playing a solo game and built a team.

Jab team strong hoti hai, systems hote hain, captain duck pe bhi chala jaaye, team jeet jaati hai. 
Business runs itself.

The real game is this:
Think big - really big
Set revenue targets that scare you
Build a team stronger than you
Create systems that work without you

Jab ye sab ho jaaye and tumhare paas koi kaam hi nahi bachta & team sambhal leti hai.
That’s the difference between a small shop and a real business. 

It’s not about mindset - it’s about structure.

Agar abhi bhi sab kuch khud kar rahe ho then you’re not running a business. You’re doing a job where you’re also the boss.

Drop a comment are you an employee in your own business, or an owner?

28.08.2026 ♥️

I didn’t celebrate my birthday this year. I celebrated myself.

For the last 5 years, I stopped celebrating my birthday. Life kept giving me reasons..family issues, personal struggles, things I was silently dealing with. And slowly, a day I once loved became a day I started dreading.

I was always that girl who LOVED birthdays.. surprises, gifts, feeling special. But this year I asked myself, why am I waiting for someone else to make me feel special?

Why do I need someone else’s plans?
Someone else’s effort?
Someone else’s presence?

So I decided… this time, I’ll do it for me.

So, just 2 days before my birthday, I booked a solo flight to Thailand. No itinerary. No proper plan. Just me.

While scrolling through reels, I saw skydiving in Thailand and randomly decided, I’m doing this.

The very next morning, at 5 AM, I left Bangkok for Pattaya.

And the funny part? I’m TERRIFIED of heights.

But maybe that’s exactly what I needed.

I’ve spent almost 30 years living in my comfort zone. This time, I wanted to face the things that scare me instead of running from them.

I want to become someone who doesn’t run away from fear but walks straight towards it.

So I jumped.

And the moment I was up there, thousands of feet above the ground, I realised…

This wasn’t just skydiving.
This was me letting go.
Letting go of the fear.
The expectations.
The disappointments.

The version of me that kept waiting for life to become perfect before allowing herself to be happy.
For someone, skydiving might just be an adventure.
For me, it was facing my fear and proving to myself that I can.

I travelled solo. I jumped solo. And I came back feeling happier and prouder than I can explain. 🤍

I didn’t share this around my birthday because nazar nahi lagwani thi 🧿 I wanted to keep this happiness to myself for a little while.

So here’s to 30.
To choosing myself.
To a new version of me.
To everything I’m leaving behind.
And to everything I’m finally brave enough to chase.
To facing my fears.

Happy Birthday to me. . 🥂🫂♥️
